title: AEA RCT Registry: social-science field-experiment denominator infrastructure
summary: The AEA RCT Registry is encoded as discipline-specific denominator infrastructure for social-science field experiments: it stores trial plans/materials, supports version history and lifecycle prompts, and embeds registry use in AEA publication policy.

status_history.note: Promoted in rev0008 as a denominator-visibility / registration-correction infrastructure record.

claims.claim: The American Economic Association maintains an RCT registry that lets investigators share work with collaborators, scholars, students, and the public by linking survey instruments, experimental findings, and experimental protocols.
what_would_change_status: AEA changes registry purpose or scope.

evidence_migration.note: rev0016 removes overloaded source_support.source_id/record_id keys and uses typed evidence_refs with ref_kind and support_role.

claims.claim: AEA says registration is free, allows amendments and added reports/articles/data/code, maintains version history, permits some hidden/embargoed fields and confidential documents, and sends lifecycle reminders such as post-trial update prompts.
what_would_change_status: AEA changes versioning, embargo/confidential-document, amendment, or reminder behavior.

evidence_migration.note: rev0016 removes overloaded source_support.source_id/record_id keys and uses typed evidence_refs with ref_kind and support_role.

claims.claim: AEA journal policy requires work involving field experiments to be registered before submission for publication, while the registry scope is randomized controlled trials in economics, political science, and other social sciences.
what_would_change_status: AEA changes field-experiment policy or registry scope.

evidence_migration.note: rev0016 removes overloaded source_support.source_id/record_id keys and uses typed evidence_refs with ref_kind and support_role.

evidence_profile.source_depth: one-pass official/institutional HTML extraction; no compliance audit, outcome evaluation, or database sampling yet
limitations: This record establishes infrastructure existence, stated purpose, process fields, and design tradeoffs; it does not estimate coverage, compliance, publication bias reduction, or outcome effects.
Registry presence is not evidence that a study was completed, well conducted, published, unpublished, null, or reported without discrepancies.

type_payload.jurisdiction_or_scope: economics, political science, and other social-science RCTs; AEA journal field-experiment submission policy
reporter_protection_design: embargoed fields and confidential documents can prevent interference with in-field surveys while preserving registry memory
limitations: lab experiments noted as not requiring registration under the cited AEA policy at retrieval
result reporting/publication linkage must be audited separately
type_payload.query_value: Lets the cube link social-science field-experiment claims to pre-analysis plans, protocols, and subsequent publication/nonpublication status.

handling_notes: Registries and post-publication platforms can make hidden or corrected research visible; they can also become instruments of reputational harm if treated as accusation surfaces.
Keep source, claim, study, result, correction, and comment separate. A platform record is not a verdict on any individual study or author.
Private, embargoed, or confidential records must not be bypassed; cite only public source metadata or ethically/lawfully available material.

unknowns: No database sampling was performed in rev0008.
Compliance, result-posting rates, selective public release, correction latency, and field-specific uptake remain open.
No individual trial, preregistration, Registered Report, retraction, or PubPeer thread record is promoted in this revision.
next_actions: Create a study-lifecycle record linking one public preregistration/registry record to its results, publication, and correction/update state.
Add compliance and coverage audits before treating any infrastructure as denominator-complete.
Add negative controls: registered studies whose records did not lead to public results, and public corrections that did not change practice.
